Because budget-spent is checked first, on the round where the budget is spent neither the wrap-up nor the pacing note is appended. The out-of-turn backstop allows 180 s for a report turn, 2100 s for a CLI head, and 2190 s for an API-key-based head; on expiry it marks the budget spent and interrupts.

requirements.title: HydraRoster.persona(at:) wraps with a double modulo and appends a round suffix past 25
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Hydra.swift:259-265 static func persona(at index: Int) - let count = personas.count; let base = personas[((index % count) + count) % count]; let round = max(0, index) / count; guard round > 0 else { return base }; return HydraPersona("\(base.name) \(round + 1)", base.asset, base.hex)
requirements.preconditions: A head has an index.
requirements.action: The persona for that index is resolved.
requirements.expected_result: Index 0-24 gives the bare roster persona. Index 25 gives "Hank 2"; index 49 gives "Gus 2"; index 50 gives "Hank 3". The suffix is a single space then the round number, which is (index / 25) + 1. The asset and hex are always the base persona's, so a later round is the same dragon in the same colour under a numbered name. A negative index wraps through the double modulo to a valid roster slot but yields an unsuffixed base name, because round is clamped by max(0, index).
requirements.persistence: None; derived from the stored index.
requirements.windows_path: JavaScript's % is already a remainder, so the double modulo must be reproduced literally; floor division must be used for round with the max(0, index) clamp.
requirements.verification_method: unit over indices -1, 0, 24, 25, 49, 50
